questions.question: On the classroom's analog clock, the hour hand is between the 7 and the 8, and the minute hand points to the 9. What time is it?
questions.explain: Each number on the clock face stands for 5 minutes, so the minute hand on the 9 means 9 × 5 = 45 minutes past. The most common trap is reading the minute hand as '9 minutes', or naming the hour the hour hand is heading toward (8) instead of the one it has already passed (7).

questions.question: Which of these shapes is a regular polygon?
options: A hexagon with all 6 sides 5 cm long and all 6 angles equal
A rectangle with two sides 8 cm long and two sides 3 cm long
A triangle with sides of 4 cm, 5 cm and 6 cm
A closed shape made of curved lines with no straight sides
questions.explain: A regular polygon is a closed shape with straight sides where ALL sides are equal AND all angles are equal. Many students pick the rectangle because its four angles are equal, but its sides are not all the same length, so it is irregular.

questions.question: On grid paper, Liam draws a rectangle that is 6 cm long and 4 cm wide. What is the perimeter of his rectangle?
questions.explain: Perimeter means the distance all the way around, so add every side: 6 + 4 + 6 + 4 = 20 cm. The classic trap is multiplying 6 × 4 = 24 (that is the area, not the perimeter) or adding only one long side and one short side.

questions.question: For an art project, Mei is cutting shapes for a border pattern. She wants a shape she can fold in half so the two halves match exactly — and it must fold that way in only ONE place. Which shape should she choose?
options: An isosceles triangle (a triangle with two equal sides)
A rectangle that is not a square
questions.explain: Test each shape with the fold: an isosceles triangle matches only when folded down the middle between its two equal sides, so it has exactly 1 line of symmetry. The trap is that the square (4 lines), the rectangle (2 lines) and the circle (many lines) all fold nicely too — but in more than one place.

questions.question: At the ferry terminal, the schedule board shows the next sailing at 19:05. Jonah's little sister asks what that time would look like on their 12-hour kitchen clock. What should he tell her?
questions.explain: For 24-hour times of 13:00 or later, subtract 12 hours and label it p.m.: 19 − 12 = 7, so 19:05 is 7:05 p.m. A very common mistake is subtracting 10 instead of 12 (giving 9:05 p.m.), or keeping the right number but forgetting that anything after 12:00 noon is p.m.

questions.question: Sofia draws a closed shape with 5 straight sides. Two of the sides are 4 cm long and the other three sides are 6 cm long. Which description fits her shape best?
options: It is not a polygon, because the sides are not all the same length
questions.explain: Count the sides to name the polygon (5 sides = pentagon), then check the side lengths to decide regular or irregular — these sides are not all equal, so it is irregular. The trap is thinking a shape must have equal sides to be a polygon at all; irregular shapes are still polygons as long as they are closed and made of straight sides.

questions.question: Ava is building a rectangular garden box at her community garden. The long sides are 300 cm and the short sides are 200 cm. She wants wooden edging all the way around the box, and the edging costs $4 for each metre. How much will the edging cost?
questions.explain: First find the perimeter: 300 + 200 + 300 + 200 = 1000 cm, then convert to metres (1000 cm = 10 m) before multiplying: 10 × $4 = $40. The two biggest traps are forgetting the cm → m conversion (which gives a wild answer like $4000) and multiplying the two side lengths to get area instead of adding all four sides.

questions.question: A carved cedar plaque at Nadia's school is a rectangle, 40 cm long and 20 cm wide. Nadia says it has 4 lines of symmetry: two folds through the middle, plus two folds from corner to corner. Is she right?
options: Yes — a rectangle has 4 lines of symmetry.
No — it has 2. Only the two folds through the middles of opposite sides make the halves match exactly.
No — it has 1. Only the fold across the short way makes the halves match exactly.
No — it has 0. A rectangle cannot be folded so that the halves match.
questions.explain: A fold is a line of symmetry only if the two halves land exactly on top of each other, so test each fold: both middle folds work, but a corner-to-corner (diagonal) fold on a 40 cm by 20 cm rectangle leaves long thin triangles sticking out. The most common misconception is borrowing the square's 4 lines of symmetry — only a square's diagonals are lines of symmetry.
